text:
mira: Heads up — discovered ~120 snapshots in s3://redwood-prod-db-backups uploaded last night without SSE-KMS (they show AES256). Names like snapshots/db-prod-20260320-22.tar.gz. Need quick triage, anyone touch uploader IAM?

adrian: Not me but I'll check CloudTrail and role diffs.

encops-bot: [alert] S3 object metadata anomaly detected — 120 objects missing SSE-KMS in redwood-prod-db-backups. Investigation id: INV-2026-03-20-01.

sam: Quick check, ran head-object on one file: `aws s3api head-object --bucket redwood-prod-db-backups --key snapshots/db-prod-20260320-22.tar.gz` shows ServerSideEncryption: AES256. So uploaded with SSE-S3.

lucy: From compliance POV this is high priority (SOC2). Are those customer-facing snapshots or internal only? Any PII touched?

mira: Likely customer tenant snapshots — need scope. Adrian can you pull CloudTrail PUT events and confirm which principal did the uploads? Also check KMS grant history — maybe kms:Encrypt permission got dropped.

adrian: CloudTrail shows an oncall change yesterday renaming role `role/backups-uploader` -> `role/backups-uploader-v2` around 21:50 UTC. The new role diff looks almost identical but I see the `kms:Encrypt` statement is missing from the assumed-role policy binding. Pulling more.

sam: Correlating timestamps: uploads from `arn:aws:sts::111:assumed-role/backups-uploader-v2` between 22:00–23:30 UTC. Matches snapshot timestamps.

lucy: We need a timeline, blast radius, and notification plan. Also detect if any restores/downloads happened — query logs for GetObject/RestoreObject in that window.

mira: Proposed playbook steps: 1) Halt uploader service (prevent further bad uploads). 2) Re-add kms:Encrypt to role and confirm KMS key policy allows the role. 3) Run a small re-encrypt job (copy with SSE-KMS) for a sample set; then scale. 4) Run restore tests against re-encrypted objects. 5) Update incident ticket and compliance brief. 6) Consider retroactive copy vs re-upload depending on size/cost.

adrian: For re-encrypt we can use S3 copy-in-place with metadata directive REPLACE. Example CLI:

```
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-prod-db-backups/snapshots/db-prod-20260320-22.tar.gz \
  s3://redwood-prod-db-backups/snapshots/db-prod-20260320-22.tar.gz \
  --metadata-directive REPLACE \
  --server-side-encryption aws:kms \
  --sse-kms-key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111:key/abcd-1234
```

Note: this issues a new PUT (counts against PUT rate) and will read the object (charges). Confirm KMS key id and key policy.

sam: Agree — schedule throttled workers so we don't spike PUTs or KMS QPS. Also confirm the key policy allows `s3.amazonaws.com` and the uploader role has `kms:Encrypt`. If we need to re-encrypt many TB, consider performing region-local parallelism and rate limits.

mira: I'll open an incident ticket and start communications. Creating INC-1873 and tagging you all. I'll also mark the affected objects as "unencrypted-at-rest" in the ticket for audit.

lucy: I'll draft a compliance note and notify legal if PII exposure is possible. Also let's add a detection rule: CloudWatch/EventBridge filter for PutObject where `s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption != aws:kms` and trigger PagerDuty if count > 5 in 15m.

adrian: Short-term mitigations: 1) Re-add kms:Encrypt to backups-uploader-v2 role. 2) Apply bucket policy deny for PutObject when `s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption != aws:kms`. Example snippet: 

```
{
  "Sid":"RequireKMSEncryption",
  "Effect":"Deny",
  "Principal":"*",
  "Action":"s3:PutObject",
  "Resource":"arn:aws:s3:::redwood-prod-db-backups/*",
  "Condition":{
    "StringNotEquals":{
      "s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption":"aws:kms"
    }
  }
}
```
This will block future non-KMS uploads (test in staging first).

sam: Also check backup-uploader CI templates — ensure they set `--server-side-encryption aws:kms` and `--sse-kms-key-id` on any uploads. Add an integration test to assert objects in test bucket use SSE-KMS.

mira: Plan: run small dry-run re-encrypt for 10 objects (1h ETA), then scale if all good. I'll update INC-1873 with progress and assign adrian/sam for remediation. If any object contains PII, we'll notify customers per policy. @lucy please prepare the compliance summary.

encops-bot: INC-1873 created by mira. Status: triage. Assigned: adrian, sam. ETA first re-encrypt run: ~1h.
